workflow_title: IMRT patient-specific measurement-based QA (gamma analysis against tolerance and action limits)
occupation_scope: Medical physicist (radiation oncology)
workflow_summary: Before an IMRT or VMAT course begins, the medical physicist measures the planned dose distribution with an independent detector and compares measured against planned dose through gamma analysis, classifying results against tolerance and action limits and acting on failures before first treatment.
source_reference: Primary: AAPM Task Group 218, Tolerance limits and methodologies for IMRT measurement-based verification QA, Medical Physics 45(4):e53-e83 (2018), DOI 10.1002/mp.12810, publication page https://mdanderson.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/tolerance-limits-and-methodologies-for-imrt-measurement-based-ver/ (verified, abstract-level): the report provides tolerance limits and methodologies for IMRT verification QA, including gamma criteria, distance-to-agreement, and required steps when plans exceed limits. Supporting: full text DOI page https://aapm.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002%2Fmp.12810 (search-confirmed, not fetched).
expert_raw_materials: Treatment plan DICOM RT-Dose export; linear accelerator log files; measurement devices (film, ion chamber, diode array, EPID portal dosimetry)
usage_permissions: Hospital QA program under national radiation-protection licensing; TG-218 openly published by AAPM; commercial TPS and detector-software licenses
task_input: An approved IMRT/VMAT treatment plan for one patient
professional_operations: Export planned dose; deliver each field or arc onto a detector phantom; capture measured dose; compute gamma map against plan using dose-difference and distance-to-agreement criteria; score against tolerance and action limits; investigate and re-plan on action-limit failure; archive the QA record
expected_deliverable: Signed per-patient QA report with gamma pass rates, failure analysis and clinical decision, filed in the treatment record
success_criteria: All treated plans pass tolerance limits; every action-limit failure resolved and re-verified before first fraction
verification_approach: Independent second-physicist review of QA reports; periodic external audits and TG-218 benchmark checks of the local QA program
platform_dependencies: Linear accelerator with record-and-verify; 2D/3D detector arrays; TPS export; gamma-analysis software (commercial Eclipse and portal dosimetry are Windows-centric; open Python replacements such as PyMedPhys run on Linux)
blocking_risks: Proprietary TPS and portal-dosimetry components are Windows-only and must be swapped for open equivalents; regulated clinical software requires validation before use; linac and detector hardware cannot be virtualized
expert_capability: Clinical dosimetry, plan interpretation, and failure troubleshooting inside a regulated medical environment
cross_domain_overlap: A medicine/oncology cluster would own treatment planning itself; this row is the measurement-verification QA standard, distinct from planning and delivery design
granularity_check: Bounded professional task: one QA cycle per patient plan, recurring daily in every IMRT clinic
pending_confirmation: TG-218 full text is paywalled; verification used the university-hosted publication page and abstract. Confirm section-level tolerance values with an AAPM member if the validator requires

workflow_title: Evaluation and reporting of measurement uncertainty per the GUM
occupation_scope: Metrologist; calibration laboratory scientist; medical physicist using dosimetry calibrations
workflow_summary: For a measurement or calibration result, the metrologist builds the measurement model, lists and quantifies all uncertainty contributions, propagates them to a combined standard uncertainty, expands to a coverage interval, and reports the result per the GUM.
source_reference: Primary: BIPM JCGM publications page https://www.bipm.org/en/committees/jc/jcgm/publications (verified): lists the GUM (JCGM 100:2008) and its supplements, maintained by the Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology whose members are BIPM, IEC, IFCC, ILAC, ISO, IUPAC, IUPAP and OIML. The GUM full text is a PDF (not fetchable in this environment).
expert_raw_materials: Instrument calibration certificates, repeatability datasets, manufacturer specifications, reference standards with stated uncertainties
usage_permissions: GUM published free of charge by the JCGM; laboratory operations under ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation
task_input: A measurement result or calibration assignment with raw data and instrument information
professional_operations: Define measurand and measurement model; identify uncertainty sources (Type A statistical and Type B other); evaluate each standard uncertainty; combine with sensitivity coefficients; compute combined standard uncertainty; expand with coverage factor k; state result with uncertainty and reporting interval
expected_deliverable: Calibration certificate or measurement report with a complete uncertainty budget
success_criteria: Report survives accreditation-body audit; results consistent in interlaboratory comparisons
verification_approach: Cross-check against a second GUM implementation (e.g. Metas.UncLib) or hand calculation; peer review of the uncertainty budget; interlaboratory comparison exercises
platform_dependencies: Method is tool-agnostic; open Python libraries (uncertainties, PyGUM, Metas.UncLib) or spreadsheets suffice; no special hardware
blocking_risks: Type B evaluations rest on documented expert judgment that resists blind automation; accredited certificates require professional signature
expert_capability: Metrology: uncertainty-budget construction, sensitivity analysis, defensible Type B estimates

granularity_check: Bounded professional task: one budget per measurement or calibration result, a recurring deliverable of metrology practice

workflow_title: Quantitative phase analysis of portland cement and clinker by X-ray powder diffraction with Rietveld refinement
occupation_scope: Analytical chemist; X-ray diffraction analyst; cement plant quality-control chemist
workflow_summary: A laboratory quantitatively determines cement phase composition by collecting an X-ray powder diffraction pattern, Rietveld-refining structure models of each phase, and reporting mass fractions of alite, belite, aluminate, ferrite and minor phases, with precision and bias controlled against certified reference clinkers.

Supporting: RELION documentation (https://relion.readthedocs.io/en/latest/, fetched HTTP 200) distributes the standard reconstruction software under GPLv2 free for commercial use and ships a single-particle tutorial for RELION-5.1; wwPDB validation-report page as in life_biomol_wf01.
expert_raw_materials: Raw cryo-EM movie frames and motion-corrected micrographs; particle stacks and coordinates; 2D classes; 3D maps including full, half, and sharpened maps plus masks; FSC curves; the atomic model built into the map.
usage_permissions: EMDB and PDB archive files are CC0 1.0 Public Domain Dedication per wwPDB policy (https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy, fetched HTTP 200); raw movie data deposited to EMPIAR are governed by EMPIAR distribution terms; RELION is GPLv2 open source (https://relion.readthedocs.io/en/latest/, fetched HTTP 200) and cryoSPARC requires a license from Structura Bio.
task_input: Vitrified purified macromolecular complex imaged as movie stacks on a cryo-transmission electron microscope.
professional_operations: Motion correction and CTF estimation; particle picking and extraction; 2D classification; ab initio reconstruction and 3D classification and refinement; map sharpening and local resolution estimation; atomic model building and refinement into the map; FSC-based and model validation; deposition of maps, half-maps, masks, and models to EMDB/OneDep per the community archiving recommendations.
expected_deliverable: A validated cryo-EM map with resolution estimate plus an atomic model, deposited to the EMDB and PDB with an accepted validation report.
success_criteria: The map resolves expected secondary structure at the stated resolution, FSC and half-map checks pass wwPDB validation, and the deposited entry is released with its validation report.
verification_approach: Inspect FSC curves and half-map agreement, local resolution, model-to-map cross-validation, and the independent wwPDB validation report; compare with known homologous structures.
platform_dependencies: RELION or cryoSPARC on Linux GPU clusters (CUDA); access to a cryo-TEM facility and detector; large fast storage for movie and particle stacks; EMDB/OneDep deposition services.
blocking_risks: Instrument access and sample vitrification are facility-bound steps; reconstruction scales with GPU clusters but remains automatable; expert classification and model-to-map judgment is difficult to automate end to end.
expert_capability: Cryo-EM image-processing knowledge, map-to-model fitting skill, and mastery of the community validation and deposit norms.
cross_domain_overlap: Shares PDB/EMDB deliverables with X-ray crystallography (life_biomol_wf01) but differs in experimental input and reconstruction mathematics; distinct from cell_imaging (life_cellimg) whose objects are cells and tissues rather than purified single particles.
granularity_check: A bounded recurring project-scale workflow of days to weeks per target; not a career and not a single alignment command.
pending_confirmation: None blocking; the 47-expert community recommendations document the archival, validation, and deposition chain end to end; reconstruction upstream steps rest on the RELION single-particle tutorial as tooling support.
data_usage_authorization: Deposited maps and models are CC0 1.0 (https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy, fetched HTTP 200); raw micrographs enter EMPIAR under its deposition agreement; RELION GPLv2 permits commercial use; cryoSPARC users hold a Structura Bio license.
privacy_considerations: Purified protein complexes are typically not personal data, but structures derived from human patient samples can become identifying via provenance; EU law classes human genetic data from a biological sample as personal data, GDPR Art 4(13) (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/, fetched HTTP 200).
research_ethics: Recombinant and cellular sample production rarely involves human subjects; human-derived material requires consent and ethics committee approval per Helsinki paragraphs 23 and 32 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/, fetched HTTP 200); animal-derived targets follow institutional animal-welfare review.
reproducibility_assessment: High post-deposition reproducibility because maps, half-maps, masks, and validation reports are public and CC0; raw-data archiving under the community recommendations makes full recomputation increasingly possible.
primary_claim: A 47-expert community consensus documents the complete cryo-EM single-particle analysis archiving, validation, and deposition workflow as the professional standard.

workflow_title: All-atom molecular dynamics simulation of a biomolecular system with equilibration, production sampling, and trajectory analysis
occupation_scope: Computational chemist; molecular modeler
workflow_summary: The full molecular dynamics workflow of preparing a protein system with topology, solvation, and ions, then energy minimization, NVT/NPT equilibration, production sampling, and analysis of structural and dynamic observables, as documented in the LiveCoMS GROMACS tutorial suite.
source_reference: Primary: Lemkul, 'From Proteins to Perturbed Hamiltonians: A Suite of Tutorials for the GROMACS-2018 Molecular Simulation Package', LiveCoMS 1(1):5068 (2019), DOI 10.33011/livecoms.1.1.5068, CC-BY 4.0, fetched HTTP 200 at https://livecomsjournal.org/index.php/livecoms/article/view/v1i1e5068: seven complete peer-reviewed tutorials from system preparation through energy minimization, equilibration, production runs, and analysis up to free-energy methods. Supporting: the living companion tutorial at http://www.mdtutorials.com/gmx/lysozyme/index.html (fetched HTTP 200, updated for GROMACS 2025.2).
expert_raw_materials: PDB starting structure; force-field topology and parameter files; water and ion model parameters; trajectory (XTC/TRR) and energy (EDR) files; analysis tool documentation.
usage_permissions: GROMACS is free open-source software under LGPL; the LiveCoMS tutorial is CC-BY 4.0 (https://livecomsjournal.org/index.php/livecoms/article/view/v1i1e5068); starting structures from the PDB are CC0 1.0 (https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy, fetched HTTP 200).
task_input: An atomic structure of the target biomolecule plus a simulation objective such as sampling time and the observables to compute.
professional_operations: Build topology and solvate the system; add counterions; energy minimize; equilibrate in NVT then NPT ensembles; run production MD; check stability and convergence metrics; compute observables such as RMSD, RMSF, SASA, contacts, or free energies.
expected_deliverable: Equilibrated production trajectories plus a written analysis of structural and dynamic observables answering the scientific question.
success_criteria: Potential energy and temperature/pressure stabilize, backbone RMSD plateaus, observables converge across replicate trajectories, and results agree with benchmarks or experiment where available.
verification_approach: Inspect convergence plots; compare computed observables against experimental or literature values; repeat with different initial velocities.
platform_dependencies: GROMACS on Linux (open source); CPU clusters suffice for small systems with GPUs for large ones; tens of GB per trajectory; visualization tools for inspection.
blocking_risks: Force-field accuracy and sampling-cost limits remain scientific risks; the pipeline itself runs natively on Linux, but convergence judgment and force-field choice are expert calls not fully automatable.
expert_capability: Simulation methodology training spanning force fields, integrators, thermostat/barostat choice, equilibration protocols, and convergence diagnostics.
cross_domain_overlap: Consumes structures produced by life_biomol_wf01/wf02/wf05; overlaps systems_microbial only at the level of whole-cell or pathway modeling which is network-scale rather than atomistic; distinct because this workflow is atomic-resolution physics.
granularity_check: A bounded recurring task at day-to-week runtime scale per system; it is neither a career nor a single simulation command.
pending_confirmation: None blocking; the peer-reviewed tutorial suite documents the whole workflow. If the merge review requires a professional-body rather than a journal as the E1 bearer, downgrade to E3.
data_usage_authorization: GROMACS LGPL open source; LiveCoMS tutorial content CC-BY 4.0 (https://livecomsjournal.org/index.php/livecoms/article/view/v1i1e5068, fetched HTTP 200); input structures CC0 1.0 from the PDB (https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy, fetched HTTP 200).
privacy_considerations: Structure coordinates for proteins are not personal data by themselves; where systems model proteins traced to identifiable human donors, EU GDPR Art 4(13) genetic-data classification can attach to the provenance metadata (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/, fetched HTTP 200).
research_ethics: No new biological samples are handled in silico; when the modeled target originates from human sample-based research, that upstream study required consent and committee approval per Helsinki paragraphs 23 and 32 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/, fetched HTTP 200).
reproducibility_assessment: Highly reproducible because the engine, force fields, and tutorials are open and versioned and trajectories are archivable; exact reruns need the same force-field version and initial velocities, and stochastic sampling demands replicate reporting.
primary_claim: A peer-reviewed LiveCoMS tutorial suite documents the complete standard GROMACS workflow from system preparation through equilibration and production to analysis, establishing the professional practice.

workflow_title: Structure-based virtual screening by molecular docking of a ligand library against a protein target
occupation_scope: Computational chemist; structure-based drug discovery scientist
workflow_summary: Prepare a curated target structure, set up grids or search space, dock a compound library with the AutoDock suite, cluster and rank poses, and validate the protocol by redocking a known ligand before screening, as specified in the Nature Protocols AutoDock procedure.
source_reference: Primary: Forli et al., 'Computational protein-ligand docking and virtual drug screening with the AutoDock suite', Nat Protoc 11(5):905-919 (2016), DOI 10.1038/nprot.2016.051, PMID 27077332, read in full at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4868550/ (fetched HTTP 200): six protocols spanning single docking with AutoDock 4 and Vina through virtual screening via Raccoon2 on Linux clusters with PBS/SGE schedulers, using the c-Abl kinase and imatinib system (PDB 1iep) as the worked example, including ligand PDBQT preparation, clustering, and screening analysis. Supporting: RCSB PDB usage policy page for structure licensing at https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy (fetched HTTP 200).
expert_raw_materials: Target PDB structure; the screening compound library (the protocol tutorial uses a 499-compound ZINC-derived NCIdivII subset); known binder poses for validation; grid maps and docking parameters.
usage_permissions: The AutoDock suite (AutoDock4, Vina, AutoDockTools, Raccoon2) is free open-source software from The Scripps Research Institute; ZINC compound downloads are governed by ZINC and upstream vendor terms; PDB structures are CC0 1.0 (https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy, fetched HTTP 200).
task_input: A target structure with curated protonation, cofactors, and waters plus a small-molecule library for screening.
professional_operations: Coordinate curation and PDBQT preparation (protonation states, metal charges, alternate conformations); define grids or search box; redock a known binder to validate the protocol; dock the library; cluster poses; rank by score and ligand efficiency; inspect key interactions of the top hits.
expected_deliverable: A ranked virtual hit list with pose files, docking scores, and a protocol report naming the top compounds for purchase or synthesis.
success_criteria: The known binder reproduces its crystallographic pose (the protocol example reproduces the imatinib pose at higher exhaustiveness), actives enrich the top-ranked fraction in control runs, and top hits show plausible ligand efficiency and interactions.
verification_approach: Redocking RMSD against the crystal pose; enrichment of known actives in the top fraction; visual and interaction plausibility checks; rerun at higher exhaustiveness for shortlisted poses.
platform_dependencies: AutoDock and Vina on Linux; screening parallelizes over clusters with PBS/SGE schedulers per the protocol; AutoDockTools GUI for preparation with batch-script alternatives documented in the paper.
blocking_risks: Docking scores carry roughly 2-3 kcal/mol error and cannot guarantee binding; the rigid-receptor approximation limits accuracy beyond a few flexible side chains; the durable expertise sits in curation and hit triage, not the pipeline itself.
expert_capability: Medicinal and computational chemistry judgment on protonation states, coordinate curation, pose plausibility, and score interpretation.
cross_domain_overlap: Adjacent to the S1-01-moved lenacapavir SAR/modeling archetype now living in biomolecular per S1_01_CATEGORY_MAPPING.csv; this workflow is the library-scale virtual screening loop while that one is the single-lead SAR table-extraction loop, so both stand; it also consumes structures from life_biomol_wf01/wf02/wf05 and target sequences from life_genom.
granularity_check: A bounded recurring screen-plus-validation workflow of hours-to-days per campaign; it is neither a career nor a single dock command.
pending_confirmation: None blocking; the protocol documents the whole workflow end to end. If the merge review treats a 2016 methods paper as too narrow a bearer of E1, downgrade to E3.
data_usage_authorization: AutoDock suite is free open source (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4868550/, fetched HTTP 200); PDB structures CC0 1.0 (https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy, fetched HTTP 200); ZINC compound downloads under ZINC and the upstream vendor terms.
privacy_considerations: Human protein target structures are not personal data on their own; provenance metadata linking a target to an identifiable donor can constitute genetic data under GDPR Art 4(13) in the EU (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/, fetched HTTP 200).
research_ethics: The workflow is fully in silico so no human or animal subjects are involved; where the target structure derives from human sample-based research, that upstream work required consent and committee approval per Helsinki paragraphs 23 and 32 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/, fetched HTTP 200).
reproducibility_assessment: Scriptable and reproducible in principle because the tools are open and the protocol published; the stochastic search means exact score reproduction needs fixed settings and the protocol requires redocking validation for each new target.
primary_claim: A Nature Protocols article documents the complete professional docking and virtual screening workflow with the AutoDock suite, from coordinate preparation to validated screening analysis, as a published standard procedure.

workflow_title: Protein structure prediction with AlphaFold2-class models and confidence-based quality assessment
occupation_scope: Structural bioinformatician; computational biologist
workflow_summary: Predict a protein's 3D structure from sequence by MSA generation and AlphaFold2 or RoseTTAFold inference, then rank the models by pLDDT, PAE, and predicted TM scores and issue a confidence-based quality assessment before any downstream use.
source_reference: Primary: Mirdita et al., 'ColabFold: making protein folding accessible to all', Nat Methods 19(6):679-682 (2022), DOI 10.1038/s41592-022-01488-1, read in full at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9184281/ (fetched HTTP 200): MMseqs2 MSA generation against UniRef30, PDB70, and ColabFoldDB, AlphaFold2 or RoseTTAFold inference, ranking of single chains by pLDDT and of complexes by PAE and predicted or interface TM scores, early-stop at mean pLDDT of 85 or higher, and the LocalColabFold CLI for Linux, macOS, and Windows WSL2 with CUDA 11.1 or later. Supporting: AlphaFold code license upstream at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/main/LICENSE (fetched HTTP 200, Apache 2.0); the professional quality-assessment gate beyond the metric layer is assembled from these partial sources, hence E3.
expert_raw_materials: Input FASTA sequences; MSA and template-hit files; predicted model PDBs with pLDDT and PAE JSON; local sequence databases (ColabFoldDB or BFD/MGnify).
usage_permissions: ColabFold is free open-source software (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9184281/, fetched HTTP 200); AlphaFold2 code is Apache 2.0 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/main/LICENSE, fetched HTTP 200); model parameter distribution terms were not verifiable this session; PDB template structures are CC0 1.0 (https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy, fetched HTTP 200).
task_input: One or more protein amino-acid sequences in FASTA, with optional custom MSA input.
professional_operations: Choose notebook or local batch mode; run MSA generation and template search; run inference; rank models by mean pLDDT; inspect PAE plots and CMSA depth and diversity diagnostics; judge confidence per domain and flag disordered regions; optionally relax and visualize; interpret biological relevance.
expected_deliverable: Ranked predicted 3D models with confidence metrics and a quality assessment stating which regions are reliable and which are not.
success_criteria: Mean pLDDT and PAE meet domain reliability thresholds (the protocol early-stops at mean pLDDT 85 or higher), predictions match experimental structures where available (the paper reports CASP14 mean TM scores around 0.886 to 0.888 versus AlphaFold2's 0.888), and low-confidence regions are correctly flagged.
verification_approach: Compare against an experimental homologue or a new X-ray or cryo-EM structure when one exists; check MSA depth against confidence; benchmark against CASP-style scores; wet-lab validation of key regions.
platform_dependencies: LocalColabFold on Linux with a CUDA 11.1+ GPU, the free Colab notebooks, or a computing cluster; local database builds need roughly 84 GB RAM for BFD/MGnify; model weight downloads.
blocking_risks: The prediction run is scriptable end to end, but interpreting low-confidence regions and biological context is expert judgment that resists automation; database snapshots and GPU procurement are operational concerns.
expert_capability: Structural bioinformatics: MSA diagnostics, confidence-metric interpretation, and protein biochemistry to judge context.
cross_domain_overlap: Feeds predicted structures into life_biomol_wf03 (MD) and life_biomol_wf04 (docking); sequence inputs come from life_genom; distinct because the deliverable is a predicted atomic model with confidence, not sequence interpretation.
granularity_check: A bounded recurring prediction-and-assessment task of minutes to days per run; it is neither a career nor a single model output.
pending_confirmation: UniProt database licensing is unverified (https://www.uniprot.org/help/license returns a JavaScript fallback with no text in this environment) and AlphaFold2 model parameter distribution terms were not fetched; confirm both with the UniProt helpdesk and with DeepMind's published parameter licensing page.
data_usage_authorization: ColabFold free open source (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9184281/, fetched HTTP 200); AlphaFold code Apache 2.0 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-deepmind/alphafold/main/LICENSE, fetched HTTP 200); PDB template structures CC0 1.0 (https://www.rcsb.org/pages/usage-policy, fetched HTTP 200); UniProt-derived database terms unverified.
privacy_considerations: A sequence alone is usually not personal data, but sequences with sample provenance or rare alleles can re-identify; in the EU human genetic data derived from a biological sample is personal data under GDPR Art 4(13) (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/, fetched HTTP 200); US clinical contexts may additionally trigger HIPAA.
research_ethics: No samples are handled; prediction relies on public sequence archives whose original clinical collection required consent per Helsinki paragraph 32 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/, fetched HTTP 200); predicted structures must not be reported as experimental evidence.
reproducibility_assessment: Reproducible given the same ColabFold version, database snapshot, and model parameters because inference is near-deterministic; rolling database versions mean exact reruns need snapshots.
primary_claim: ColabFold documents the complete prediction run of MSA generation, AlphaFold2 or RoseTTAFold inference, and pLDDT or PAE ranking with a free Linux toolchain, while the professional quality-assessment gate is assembled from this and community practice.

Its object is sequence-level evidence: assemblies, variant calls, expression measurements, and their quality certificates, produced from sequencing-instrument outputs (Illumina, PacBio, ONT). It is separated from biomolecular (atomic-structure-level work) because its outputs are sequences, not structures; from cell_imaging because its evidence is reads and counts rather than images; from systems_microbial because it stops at a single genome or transcriptome rather than modelling whole organisms, communities, or regulatory networks.

workflow_title: Clinical germline sequence variant interpretation and reporting per ACMG/AMP standards and guidelines
occupation_scope: Clinical molecular geneticist; molecular genetic pathologist; variant curation scientist in a certified diagnostic laboratory
workflow_summary: A board-certified clinical genetics professional takes a patient's germline sequence variants (NGS panel, exome, or genome), scores each against the ACMG/AMP evidence criteria using reference transcripts, population frequency, functional prediction, segregation, and literature, assigns one of five classification tiers, and writes a clinical report returned to the ordering clinician with variant interpretations deposited to ClinVar.
source_reference: Primary: Richards et al., Standards and guidelines for the interpretation of sequence variants, Genet Med 17(5):405-424, 2015, PMID 25741868, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4544753/ (fetched HTTP 200, read in full; joint ACMG+AMP+CAP workgroup standard documenting the whole classify-and-report workflow, evidence criterion weighting, and required professional qualifications). Supporting: NCBI policies page https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/ (fetched HTTP 200; NCBI places no restrictions on molecular database use but does not transfer submitter rights).
expert_raw_materials: Filtered variant call list (VCF) from the test pipeline; reference transcript and LRG records; population databases (ExAC, dbSNP, 1000 Genomes); disease databases (ClinVar, OMIM, HGMD); locus-specific databases; computational predictors (SIFT, PolyPhen-2, CADD, splice predictors); patient phenotype and family history from the ordering clinician
usage_permissions: ClinVar and dbSNP release data under public archival terms; HGMD is a commercial licensed database; patient-level information is handled under HIPAA-compliant clinical sharing per Richards 2015 (PMID 25741868)
task_input: A filtered germline variant list for a Mendelian- or mitochondrial-panel test plus the patient indication and family history
professional_operations: Map each variant to HGVS nomenclature on a reference transcript; gather population, computational, functional, segregation, and case-level evidence; weight evidence per the ACMG/AMP criteria (PVS1, PS1-PS4, PM1-PM6, PP1-PP5 and BA1, BS1-BS4, BP1-BP7); combine into a five-tier classification (pathogenic, likely pathogenic, uncertain significance, likely benign, benign); perform an independent second professional review; write the interpretive report; submit the interpretation to ClinVar
expected_deliverable: A signed clinical variant interpretation report with evidence codes and a final classification per variant, returned to the ordering provider, plus a ClinVar deposition where policy permits
success_criteria: Classifications follow the published criterion weighting, are reproducible by a second certified reviewer, and show inter-laboratory concordance validated through proficiency testing under the laboratory regulatory framework
verification_approach: Independent second review by a certified molecular geneticist or molecular genetic pathologist; inter-laboratory interpretation exchanges and ClinVar concordance comparisons
platform_dependencies: Variant curation platform, HGVS mapping tools (e.g. mutalyzer.nl), population and disease databases, LIMS, and a compliant clinical reporting system
blocking_risks: Board-certified sign-off and laboratory certification are legal requirements; HGMD is license-gated; patient data privacy (HIPAA in US, GDPR in EU) constrains cloud processing; labs differ in criterion weighting in borderline cases
expert_capability: Board certification in clinical molecular genetics or molecular genetic pathology plus demonstrated variant-curation judgement under ACMG/AMP standards
cross_domain_overlap: Touches med_inform_wf03 (OMOP observational study) only through shared clinical data; the neighboring somatic-molecular-profiling workflow is distinct because tumor-only variant reading follows AMP/ASCO/CAP rules, not the germline five-tier system
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded per-case interpret-and-report cycle lasting hours to a few days; not a career and not a single evidence-criterion lookup
pending_confirmation: Confirm with a certified molecular geneticist that the 2015 ACMG/AMP write-up still describes current day-to-day practice given post-2015 updates (e.g. ClinGen recommendations, AMP tumor guidance); coordinator to adjudicate E1 versus E3 if the follow-up weakens the whole-workflow claim
data_usage_authorization: ClinVar/NLM public-data reuse terms apply to population and disease annotations: NCBI places no restrictions on molecular database use but does not transfer submitter rights E1 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/); patient clinical data require HIPAA authorization or the applicable consent
privacy_considerations: Germline variants with phenotype metadata are health data identifying the patient under GDPR Art 4(13) and 4(15) in the EU E1 (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/) and are protected under HIPAA where the data is US clinical; sequence data itself can re-identify, so anonymization must be assessed case by case
research_ethics: Clinical interpretation under the lab quality framework is regulated practice rather than research; any research secondary use of patient samples requires ethics committee approval and informed consent per WMA Helsinki paras 23 and 32 E1 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/)
reproducibility_assessment: Partly reproducible: evidence criteria and HGVS mapping are explicit and repeatable, but clinical judgement weighting and licensed databases (HGMD) are operator- and license-dependent steps; the field promotes standardization through ClinVar sharing and proficiency testing E1 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4544753/)
primary_claim: The joint ACMG/AMP/CAP 2015 guidelines define the complete professional workflow for germline sequence variant interpretation: evidence criteria, five-tier classification, reporting standards, and required professional qualifications

workflow_title: RNA-seq transcriptome profiling and differential expression analysis following the community best-practices roadmap
occupation_scope: Bioinformatics scientist (genomics); NGS data analyst; core facility scientist
workflow_summary: A genomics bioinformatician designs a replicated RNA-seq experiment, quality-controls raw reads, aligns them to a reference genome or transcriptome, quantifies expression, runs normalized differential expression with negative-binomial models, checks results against community quality thresholds such as expected mapping rate, and delivers ranked gene lists with complete settings documentation.
source_reference: Primary: Conesa et al., A survey of best practices for RNA-seq data analysis, Genome Biol 17:13, 2016, PMID 26813401, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4728800/ (fetched HTTP 200, full roadmap read; community best-practices guideline covering the whole pre-analysis, core, and advanced workflow with quantitative QC norms). Supporting: NCBI policies page https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/ (fetched HTTP 200) for reference-data terms.
expert_raw_materials: RNA-seq FASTQ reads; reference genome FASTA and GTF annotation; sample metadata and experimental design table; FastQC/Trimmomatic/FASTX tools; HTSeq-count or featureCounts; DESeq2 or edgeR in R/Bioconductor
usage_permissions: Public reference genomes from NCBI/Ensembl are reusable under their open release terms; human study data reuse follows the sequencing facility data access agreement and the original participant consent
task_input: FASTQ files from a replicated sequencing run plus the experimental design (conditions, biological replicates)
professional_operations: Run raw-read QC (FastQC) and trim or discard low-quality reads (Trimmomatic/FASTX); align with a splice-aware aligner; check the mapping rate against the expected roughly 70-90 percent for human reads and run alignment QC (Picard/RSeQC/Qualimap); quantify per-gene counts (HTSeq-count/featureCounts); normalize (TMM) and fit negative-binomial differential expression (DESeq2/edgeR); validate the design with replication checks and PCA; document every tool version and setting; optionally repeat with a second package to confirm robustness
expected_deliverable: A QC report, an expression matrix, and a differentially expressed gene list with adjusted p-values, fold changes, and complete reproducible provenance

verification_approach: Cross-check with a second differential expression package; confirm QC metrics (mapping fraction, 3-prime bias, GC content) against the roadmap thresholds; PCA for batch separation
platform_dependencies: Linux HPC or cloud with splice-aware aligners, R/Bioconductor, and RAM for genome indexes; containerization for reproducibility
blocking_risks: Human FASTQ may be controlled access: EGA under GDPR in the EU, dbGaP in the US E3 (registration pages blocked to this environment, cited from public documentation); batch effects and strandedness miscalibration produce false DE; the 2016 benchmarks predate pseudoalignment tools

workflow_title: De novo genome assembly quality assessment using reference-free k-mer metrics for consensus quality, completeness, and phasing
occupation_scope: Genome assembly specialist; bioinformatics scientist in a genome sequencing center
workflow_summary: After a genome assembly is produced, a genome bioinformatician evaluates it reference-free: k-mers counted from unassembled high-accuracy reads are compared against the assembly to estimate consensus quality (QV), completeness, and false duplications, and with parental data the phasing statistics; the metrics, spectrum plots, and browser tracks decide whether the assembly is fit for release.
source_reference: Primary: Rhie et al., Merqury: reference-free quality, completeness, and phasing assessment for genome assemblies, Genome Biol 21:245, 2020, PMID 32928274, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7488777/ (fetched HTTP 200, read in full; methods paper defining and demonstrating the complete QC procedure on Arabidopsis and human assemblies with QV, k-mer completeness, hap-mer phasing statistics, and plot deliverables). Supporting: NCBI policies page https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/ (fetched HTTP 200).
expert_raw_materials: Assembled genome FASTA (primary and alternate haplotypes); high-accuracy unassembled reads from the same sample; optional parental assemblies or reads for trio hap-mer analysis; estimated genome size and ploidy
usage_permissions: Merqury and Meryl are free open source (github.com/marbl/merqury); assembly and read data reuse follows the owning project release terms and, for human data, the applicable data-sharing policy
task_input: A draft assembly plus high-accuracy unassembled reads, and parental data when phasing QC is required
professional_operations: Count k-mers from the reads with Meryl; run Merqury against the assembly k-mers; compute consensus QV and k-mer completeness; generate spectra-cn and spectra-asm plots; for trios compute hap-mers, phase-block NG50, and switch-error rates; interpret plots (missing-sequence black peaks, false-duplication humps, unbalanced spectra) and accept the assembly or route it back for correction (polishing, purge_dups, re-assembly)
expected_deliverable: A quality report with QV, completeness percentages, phase-block statistics, and publication-ready spectrum figures plus optional IGV tracks
success_criteria: QV at or above the acceptance band (Q30 equals 99.9 percent consensus accuracy), high k-mer completeness with balanced haplotype-specific completeness for diploid assemblies, and spectra free of unexplained missing-k-mer or duplication anomalies (a clean spectrum is necessary but not sufficient)
verification_approach: Cross-check against independent metrics such as BUSCO gene completeness and mapping-based QV, compare exact (Meryl) and approximate (Mash) QV estimates, and visually inspect spectra under the interpretation rules and the Clavijo caveat that wrong spectra prove a wrong assembly
platform_dependencies: Linux workstation or cluster with Meryl and Merqury; enough RAM for k-mer counting of large read sets; a genome browser (IGV) for tracks
blocking_risks: K-mer counting for large genomes is memory-intensive; human read sets may be controlled access (EGA under GDPR in the EU, dbGaP in the US) E3 (registration pages blocked to this environment); spectra interpretation remains a trained manual judgement step
expert_capability: Assembly-level bioinformatics: k-mer statistics, assembly pipeline literacy, and the ability to read spectrum diagnostics
cross_domain_overlap: Shares contiguity and annotation QC (BUSCO, NG50) with assembly workflows generally but is a distinct bounded quality-assurance task; no A-round candidate duplicates it
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded post-assembly QA pass of hours to a day per assembly; not the assembly itself and not a single metric computation
pending_confirmation: Confirm with a genome-center assembly specialist that Merqury-style k-mer QC is a standalone recurring deliverable in production pipelines (VGP/HPRC-class) rather than always an embedded stage; coordinator to adjudicate whether a tool-authors methods paper bears E1 or should be E3
data_usage_authorization: Tool is free open source; input reads and assemblies are reused under the data owner terms: NCBI places no restrictions on its molecular databases but does not transfer submitter rights E1 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/)
privacy_considerations: Human genome reads are genetic data under GDPR Art 4(13) in the EU E1 (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/) and typically require controlled access (EGA for EU citizens, dbGaP for NIH US data); QC of consented public reference materials (GIAB) is open, but identifying snippets must stay inside the controlled environment

reproducibility_assessment: Fully reproducible numerics: Meryl and Merqury are deterministic open tools and the paper publishes its test assemblies, so the QV and completeness tables can be recomputed exactly E1 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7488777/)
primary_claim: The Merqury paper defines and demonstrates the complete reference-free assembly quality assessment procedure (QV, k-mer completeness, false-duplication detection, trio phasing statistics, spectrum plots, browser tracks) on human and plant assemblies

workflow_title: Benchmarking a germline small-variant callset against community truth sets following GA4GH best practices
occupation_scope: Bioinformatics scientist (genomics); pipeline developer in a clinical laboratory or sequencing provider
workflow_summary: A lab bioinformatician runs the variant calling pipeline on a Genome in a Bottle reference sample, compares the resulting VCF against the public truth VCF restricted to confident regions, normalizes representation and matches variants in a tiered scheme, computes precision and recall stratified by variant type and difficult context, and produces a standardized report that certifies or rejects a pipeline version.
source_reference: Primary: Krusche et al., Best practices for benchmarking germline small-variant calls in human genomes, Nat Biotechnol 37(5):555-560, 2019, PMID 30858580, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6699627/ (fetched HTTP 200, read in full; GA4GH Benchmarking Team standard documenting the complete benchmark protocol, matching tiers, metric definitions, truth sets, and reporting). Supporting: GA4GH benchmarking-tools repository github.com/ga4gh/benchmarking-tools (cited in the paper).
expert_raw_materials: Truth VCF and confident-region BED from GIAB (or Platinum Genomes, synthetic diploid); query VCF from the pipeline under test; reference FASTA; optional stratification BEDs for GC content and repeat contexts
usage_permissions: GIAB and Platinum Genomes truth materials are public benchmark releases intended for unrestricted reuse; hap.py and the benchmarking tools are open source (github.com/ga4gh/benchmarking-tools); lab-internal query calls stay under lab policy
task_input: An unvalidated germline VCF produced by the lab pipeline on a benchmark sample
professional_operations: Normalize variant representation (left-shift and trim); compare query against truth with hap.py (vcfeval recommended as an additional comparator); apply the three-tier matching (genotype, allele, local); tally TP, FP, and FN including FP.GT and FP.AL partial credits; compute precision and recall; stratify by SNV versus indel, GC content, and repeat regions; sample and manually curate FP and FN subsets to locate pipeline defects; publish the standardized benchmark report with precision-recall curves
expected_deliverable: A standardized hap.py HTML benchmark report (stratified precision and recall, PR curves, error distributions) plus a curation log of investigated FP/FN subsets
success_criteria: Precision and recall at or above lab acceptance targets (the paper's PCR-free example reaches 99.9/99.9 percent SNV precision/recall, indel precision 99.3 and indel recall 97.1) with reproducible stratification across two benchmark samples
verification_approach: Reproduce with a second comparator (hap.py versus vcfeval agreement), rerun on a second truth sample, and have FP/FN subsets curated by a second analyst
platform_dependencies: Linux server able to run the lab pipeline; hap.py in a container with the reference FASTA and truth sets staged locally
blocking_risks: Benchmark materials are open but any incidental comparison against patient data must respect GDPR/HIPAA containment; variant representation mismatches between caller and truth dwarf real differences, so normalization handling needs care
expert_capability: VCF semantics and normalization mastery plus pipeline debugging across alignment and variant calling stages
cross_domain_overlap: Shares GIAB reference materials with the genomics variant-classification ecosystem (life_genom_wf01) but is a distinct pipeline-qualification QA workflow; no A-round duplicate among eng_, ag_, legal_, or med_ fragments
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded pipeline-qualification pass of hours per truth set; not a career and not a single hap.py command
pending_confirmation: Confirm with a clinical-bioinformatics lab director that the GA4GH best-practices protocol is the operative benchmark standard in current CAP/ISO pipeline validation; coordinator to adjudicate E1 versus E3
data_usage_authorization: GIAB truth sets are public benchmark releases intended for unrestricted reuse; NCBI hosts related materials with no restrictions on molecular data E1 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/); lab VCFs are internal data
privacy_considerations: Benchmark samples are consented, openly releasable cell-line genomes (NA12878 family), but any incidental comparison against patient data requires GDPR Art 4(13) and HIPAA containment E1 (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/)
research_ethics: GIAB reference materials derive from consented, anonymized cell lines under NIST and Coriell governance; pipeline benchmarking returns no clinical interpretation and follows the lab quality system rather than Helsinki research consent; any added research reuse needs ethics approval per Helsinki para 23 E1 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/)
reproducibility_assessment: Highly reproducible end to end: truth sets, reference, and hap.py are public, so the same pipeline version reproduces identical precision and recall; residual variation is pipeline-version and environment pinning E1 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6699627/)

workflow_title: MIFlowCyt-compliant annotation and reporting of a flow cytometry experiment for publication and public data release
occupation_scope: Flow cytometry specialist; FACS core facility staff; immunology and cell biology researchers who publish flow cytometry experiments
workflow_summary: Annotate a completed or in-preparation flow cytometry experiment according to the ISAC MIFlowCyt minimum-information standard (purpose, samples and reagents, instrument configuration, compensation, gating) and attach the compliant description to the FCS list-mode data in a journal supplement or a public repository such as ImmPort, so third parties can independently interpret, validate and reuse the experiment.
source_reference: Primary: Lee JA et al., 'MIFlowCyt: The Minimum Information about a Flow Cytometry Experiment', Cytometry A 73(10):926-930 (2008), DOI 10.1002/cyto.a.20623, PMID 18752282, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2773297/ (fetched HTTP 200, full text read): ISAC Data Standards Task Force standard vetted by the DSTF, Standards Committee and ISAC Council and endorsed by NIAID DAIT DISC, MIBBI-registered; organizes annotation into Experiment Overview, Flow Sample, Instrument Details and Data Analysis with RFC2119-style shall/should requirement levels. Supporting: ImmPort https://immport.org (cited directly by the primary as the NIAID-funded repository that adopted the MIFlowCyt framework); ISAC https://www.isac-net.org/ (cited directly by the primary as distributor of the normative standard).
expert_raw_materials: FCS list-mode data files, instrument configuration logs (light sources, filters, detector settings such as PMT voltage, flow cell type), antibody and reagent panels with catalog numbers, compensation matrices, gating trees, experimental design and sample records, controlled vocabularies (NCBI taxonomy, MeSH).
usage_permissions: The ISAC standard is publicly distributed (normative version published as supplement to the paper and available from isac-net.org per the primary); FCS data made public must be cleared for that use by the originating institution and any consent terms; ImmPort deposits are governed by NIAID-funded data-sharing plans and ImmPort access terms.
task_input: FCS list-mode data files from a flow cytometry experiment, experimental design and sample records, reagent/antibody panel details, instrument configuration logs, compensation matrices and the gating analysis.
professional_operations: Capture the Experiment Overview (purpose/goal/hypothesis, experimental variables, conclusions, quality-control measures, contact information); describe the Flow Sample (material, source organism/location, treatment, reagent/analyte/detector/reporter for each measurement such as CD25/anti-CD25/FITC); record Instrument Details (manufacturer/model when uniquely identifying, otherwise light sources, filters, laser power, PMT voltages, flow cell and detectors); document Data Analysis (FCS files provided or request path stated, compensation type and spillover matrix, gating boundaries as mathematical descriptions with denominators traceable to all events); sweep the checklist for every shall and should item; deposit the annotated dataset to a repository such as ImmPort or submit as a journal supplement.
expected_deliverable: A MIFlowCyt-compliant experiment annotation accompanying the FCS data, submitted to a journal supplement or public repository (ImmPort), with every normative shall-item satisfied.
success_criteria: An independent analyst can reconstruct the experiment and re-derive gated population statistics from the deposited FCS files: compensation matrix present, gates mathematically described, denominators stated, instrument configuration sufficient to interpret intensities, and the repository curator or reviewer accepts the annotation.
verification_approach: Checklist compliance review against the normative MIFlowCyt requirement list; independent re-gating of the deposited list-mode files; peer reviewer or editor assessment at publication; curation acceptance at ImmPort.
platform_dependencies: FCS-standard files from a flow cytometer and its acquisition software; structured annotation tooling (spreadsheet, LIMS or ontology tools); a public repository such as ImmPort or journal supplement hosting; no significant compute.
blocking_risks: Clinical or patient-derived samples may be consent-limited and cannot be publicly deposited; proprietary acquisition formats and lost instrument-configuration logs break the instrument-details requirements; annotation burden produces incomplete compliance in practice; some vendor documentation pages are bot-blocked in this environment.
expert_capability: Complete working knowledge of the experiment (design, reagents, instrument setup, gating logic) plus familiarity with the ISAC standard and repository submission requirements.
cross_domain_overlap: Analyte/reagent ontology annotation touches genomics bio-annotation but FCS cytometric events are not sequence data; clinical FCM results reporting belongs to the clinical laboratory domain and is distinct from this research-side annotation deliverable; adjacent to life_cellimg_wf04 (both share cell-level data) but wf01 covers one experiment's semantics while wf04 covers public image-archive metadata.
granularity_check: Proper granularity: a bounded recurring reporting task per experiment that ends in a citable dataset, not a career (running a cytometry core) and not a micro-action (writing a single gate description).
pending_confirmation: Confirm with the ISAC Data Standards Task Force or FlowRepository curation that MIFlowCyt-based annotation remains the operative submission model for public FCS data; E1 rests on the ISAC-adopted standard plus ImmPort adoption, and the coordinator should adjudicate whether the reporting-scope framing merits E1 rather than E3.
data_usage_authorization: E1 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2773297/): the standard requires FCS list-mode data be provided directly or a request path stated, and public deposit is bound by originating-institution consent and repository terms; ImmPort, which adopted the MIFlowCyt framework per the primary, governs deposited data under NIAID data-sharing plans.
privacy_considerations: E1 (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/): patient-derived flow data linked to a donor are personal health data under GDPR Art 4(15) (EU), and HIPAA-covered PHI where the samples are US clinical; de-identification is required before public deposit; cell-line-derived data alone are not personal data under GDPR Art 4(1).
research_ethics: E1 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/): experiments on human material require prior research-ethics-committee approval (2024 Helsinki para 23) and consent for collection, processing, storage and secondary use (para 32); established cell lines are used under institutional biosafety, authentication and mycoplasma-testing norms.
reproducibility_assessment: E1 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2773297/): the standard's stated purpose is enabling independent validation, refutation and reuse; FCS is an ISAC file-format standard and gating must be mathematically described; less reproducible in practice is instrument behavior not captured by the logged configuration.
primary_claim: An ISAC-adopted minimum-information standard specifying, with shall/should requirement levels, every annotation element (experiment overview, samples and reagents, instrument configuration, FCS data, compensation, gating) required to interpret, validate and reuse a flow cytometry experiment, adopted by the ImmPort repository for deposition workflow use.

workflow_title: Light microscope performance verification and quality control program for a core imaging facility
occupation_scope: Microscopy core facility custodian; imaging scientist responsible for instrument performance
workflow_summary: Run a recurring, protocol-driven quality control program for widefield and confocal light microscopes: measure illumination power and stability, detection-system performance, field flatness, channel co-registration, lateral and axial resolution, and stage/focus precision on a defined schedule with consensus standard samples, record trends and metadata, and correct or service deviations so that quantitative imaging results are reproducible.
source_reference: Primary: Boehm U et al., 'QUAREP-LiMi: A Community Endeavour to Advance Quality Assessment and Reproducibility in Light Microscopy', Nat Methods 18(12):1423-1426 (2021), DOI 10.1038/s41592-021-01162-y, PMID 34021279, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9443067/ (fetched HTTP 200, full text read; corrected Nat Methods 19(2):256, 2022): defines the QC program via 11 working groups (WG1 illumination power and stability with calibrated external power sensors, WG2 detection performance, WG3 field flatness, WG4 chromatic aberration and co-registration with multicolor beads, WG5 lateral/axial resolution with sub-resolution fluorescent beads, WG6 stage and focus precision, WG7 provenance and QC metadata, WG10 image quality, WG11 publication standards) and reports a 225-microscopist survey where inconsistent QC and lack of staff time are the main barriers. Supporting: QUAREP-LiMi https://quarep.org/ (cited directly by the primary as host of working-group protocols); ISO 21073:2019 confocal microscopy standard (cited directly by the primary); Global BioImaging QA recommendation PDF https://www.globalbioimaging.org/user/pages/05.documents/D2.3_Publication%20of%20common%20recommendation_quality%20assurance%20and%20management%20in%20open%20access%20imaging%20infrastructures.pdf and the BioImaging UK ISO 21073 interpretation paper (both cited directly by the primary as the confocal methodology anchors).
expert_raw_materials: Calibrated external power sensors, sub-resolution fluorescent beads, multicolor bead slides, standard test slides, ISO 21073:2019 methodology, QUAREP-LiMi working-group SOPs, instrument service and trend log sheets, acquisition-metadata records.
usage_permissions: QUAREP-LiMi protocols and guidelines are stated in the primary to be published open access; final SOPs live on quarep.org; ISO 21073:2019 is a paid ISO standard; QC software tools carry their own licenses; facility QC records are institutional property shared under facility policy.
task_input: A microscope system entering service or due for scheduled QC, or a complaint/publication requiring performance evidence; calibrated sensors, bead standards and the applicable SOP.
professional_operations: Scope the QC program for the widefield/confocal platforms; measure illumination power and short/long-term stability with calibrated external sensors (WG1); characterize detection-system performance including the emission path (WG2); assess field uniformity and flatness (WG3); measure chromatic co-registration with multicolor beads (WG4); measure lateral and axial resolution with sub-resolution fluorescent beads (WG5); test stage and focus repeatability (WG6); record results with data-provenance and QC metadata (WG7); trend metrics over time; run calibration/correction or request service for out-of-tolerance results; attach QC evidence to facility datasets and methods sections.
expected_deliverable: A dated instrument QC log with metrics, trends and corrective actions, plus QC metadata attached to datasets produced or published on the instrument.
success_criteria: Metrics stay within consensus tolerance on schedule; drift is detected before it affects data; each publication or facility dataset can cite dated QC evidence for its instrument; measurements are repeatable between operators and across sites.
verification_approach: Repeat-measurement reproducibility; comparison against the BioImaging UK methodology companion to ISO 21073:2019; participation in multi-laboratory protocol testing rounds coordinated by QUAREP-LiMi working groups; automated QC scripts where adopted.
platform_dependencies: The microscope systems themselves; calibrated sensors, bead standards and test slides; QC and analysis software (free and commercial); staff hours (identified in the survey as the main barrier); ISO 21073:2019 as confocal reference methodology.
blocking_risks: Lack of staff time is the main identified barrier; most QC tests are manual and time-consuming; protocol landscape is split across separate publications and quarep.org rather than one normative document; hardware heterogeneity across vendors means per-instrument protocols; the ISO anchor standard is paid-access.
expert_capability: An imaging scientist with enough optics and detector knowledge to run the measurements, interpret out-of-tolerance results and correct them; not a software-only skill.
cross_domain_overlap: QUAREP WG7 metadata connects to life_cellimg_wf04 (REMBI archive metadata) and the cryo-EM community runs parallel instrument/validation practice inside life_biomol_wf02; distinct because the deliverable here is instrument performance evidence, not structures or deposited datasets.
granularity_check: Proper granularity: a recurring per-instrument task with bounded scope and an audit trail; running the whole facility program is a role, the QC measurement-and-record cycle is the task.
pending_confirmation: Confirm with a QUAREP-LiMi working group chair (https://quarep.org/) which post-2021 final protocols now constitute the operative SOP set for widefield and confocal QC. E3 because the 2021 paper defines the program and working groups while the final protocols are published separately, so the whole-workflow source chain is assembled, not single-document.
data_usage_authorization: E3 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9443067/): QUAREP-LiMi outputs are published open access per the paper; ISO 21073:2019 is a paid ISO/IEC standard; software tools carry their own licenses; facility QC logs are institutional records shared under facility policy.
privacy_considerations: E1 (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/): instrument QC uses standard beads and test slides, containing no personal data; human-sample imaging later run on QC-passed instruments is governed by GDPR (EU) or HIPAA (US clinical) where it contains identifiable health data.
research_ethics: E1 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/): the QC task itself involves no human or animal subjects so Helsinki approval does not apply to it; facilities that image animals or human tissue must hold the relevant ethics and welfare approvals for those studies (2024 Helsinki paras 21, 23).
reproducibility_assessment: E1 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9443067/): the program exists to make quantitative microscopy reproducible; WG7 defines provenance and QC metadata standards; open-access protocol publication and the push toward automated QC support repeatable measurements.
primary_claim: A community initiative (formed April 2020, 256 members across 24 countries) whose 11 working groups define the scope, samples, metrics and metadata of a light-microscopy QC program, reporting that QC is currently inconsistent and manual, the main barrier being staff time.

occupation_scope: High-content screening scientist; bioimage analyst; drug-discovery and functional-genomics biologist
workflow_summary: Plate cells in multi-well plates, apply compound or genetic perturbations, stain with the six-dye five-channel Cell Painting multiplex, image on a high-throughput microscope, then run automated illumination correction, image quality control and per-cell feature extraction (about 1,500 morphological features) to build profiles that are compared across perturbations for mechanism-of-action grouping, pathway mapping and disease signatures.
source_reference: Primary: Bray MA et al., 'Cell Painting, a high-content image-based assay for morphological profiling using multiplexed fluorescent dyes', Nat Protoc 11(9):1757-1774 (2016), DOI 10.1038/nprot.2016.105, PMID 27560178, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5223290/ (fetched HTTP 200, author manuscript read through the Materials section): full assay design and workflow, six dyes in five channels marking eight cellular components (Hoechst/DNA, concanavalin A/ER, SYTO 14/nucleoli and RNA, phalloidin and WGA/actin-Golgi-membrane, MitoTracker/mitochondria), plate layout and replicate rules (at least four biological replicates recommended, about 30 control wells per 384-well plate), perturbation timings (24-48 h compounds, 96 h RNAi, 72 h overexpression), three CellProfiler pipeline stages (illumination correction, supervised-ML QC via CellProfiler Analyst, feature extraction), a two-week culture/imaging plus one-to-two-week analysis timeline, and validation at two independent sites by more than ten researchers. Supporting: CellProfiler forum http://forum.cellprofiler.org/ (cited directly by the primary as the open-source analysis software support channel).
expert_raw_materials: Cell line or primary cell cultures (U2OS and A549 most used), compound libraries or genetic-reagent sets, the six-dye reagent panel, multi-well plates, high-throughput automated microscope images, CellProfiler pipelines, illumination-correction maps, QC classifier training images, downstream profile matrices and compound/gene annotations.
usage_permissions: CellProfiler and CellProfiler Analyst are open source per the primary; reagent catalog items are commercial purchases; small-molecule or siRNA libraries may carry vendor MTA restrictions; resulting public profile datasets are governed by the hosting repository's terms; archived images follow repository licenses.
task_input: A perturbation set (compounds at chosen concentrations or RNAi/overexpression reagents), a chosen adherent cell line, an experimental question (mechanism of action, pathway grouping, disease phenotypic signature).
professional_operations: Test and select the cell type (adherent, monolayer-forming, about 80 percent confluence at fixation) and seeding density in a pilot; design the plate layout with spatially scattered replicates and controls (chevron control pattern); apply perturbations for the modality-appropriate duration; fix, permeabilize and stain with the six-dye multiplex; image five channels on a high-throughput microscope; run per-plate per-channel illumination correction; run supervised-machine-learning image QC and discard aberrant images; extract about 1,500 morphology, intensity, texture and adjacency features per cell with CellProfiler; aggregate and control-normalize profiles; compare profiles across perturbations (clustering, target/mechanism matching, disease signature recovery); archive images and report hits and signatures.
expected_deliverable: Morphological profiles (about 1,500 features per cell) for every perturbation plus an analysis report of hits, pathway clusters or disease-signature matches, with the underlying images archived.
success_criteria: Annotated compounds of known mechanism cluster by mode of action; negative (vehicle) controls do not separate by batch or plate; QC keeps the failed-image fraction low; profiles detect subtle phenotypes at single-cell resolution; replicate concordance holds across the four or more replicates.
verification_approach: Replicate concordance checks; positive and negative control behavior; profile similarity against published compound annotations; cross-check of hit mechanisms in the literature; the protocol itself was validated at two independent sites (Broad Institute and Recursion Pharmaceuticals) by more than ten researchers.
platform_dependencies: High-throughput automated microscope and automated plate handling; CellProfiler pipelines (per the primary a desktop suffices below roughly 1,000 images, a computing cluster is needed beyond); supervised QC training via CellProfiler Analyst; cell-culture infrastructure; cluster and IT support for large campaigns.
blocking_risks: Statistical analysis of a roughly 1,500-dimensional feature space (curse of dimensionality, overfitting, multiple testing) is flagged by the authors as a challenge; cross-experiment batch normalization protocols were not yet established at publication; RNAi off-target effects inhibit gene comparisons; large campaigns need cluster and IT resources; equipment and cell-culture expertise required.
expert_capability: Combined cell biology, automated screening and image-analysis expertise; feature extraction is automated but experimental design, QC judgment and profile interpretation are expert tasks.
cross_domain_overlap: Compound library work also appears in biomolecular virtual screening (life_biomol_wf04) but there the readout is docking scores on protein structures, here it is image-based phenotypes, so the two are distinct modalities; high-content imaging touches clinical histopathology (S1-02B med_diag_wf03 synoptic reporting) but this is research-side perturbation profiling, not diagnosis.
granularity_check: Proper granularity: one bounded assay campaign of roughly two to four weeks defined by a step protocol, not a career and not a single stain or imaging action.
pending_confirmation: E1 framing rests on a Nature Protocols complete protocol; only the author manuscript (truncated during the Materials section) was read in this environment, so the coordinator should confirm the publisher Procedure steps match the workflow claims before final E1 sign-off.
data_usage_authorization: E1 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5223290/): the analysis software (CellProfiler) is open source per the paper; cell lines are obtained under vendor (ATCC) material terms with authentication and mycoplasma-check obligations flagged in the protocol; any public release of profile data or images is governed by the hosting repository's terms and the originating institution's data policies.
privacy_considerations: E1 (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/): images and profiles of established cell lines are not personal data under GDPR Art 4(1); where primary human cells are used (the protocol supports primary fibroblasts and hepatocyte co-cultures), donor-linked samples and derived profiles are personal health data governed by GDPR (EU) or HIPAA (US clinical) and require de-identification before sharing.
research_ethics: E1 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/): work with primary human material requires research-ethics-committee approval (2024 Helsinki para 23) and consent for storage and secondary use (para 32); established cell lines are used under institutional biosafety rules, and the protocol requires regular cell-line authentication and mycoplasma testing.
reproducibility_assessment: E1 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5223290/): the protocol was implemented at two independent sites by more than ten researchers, CellProfiler pipelines are open source, and replicate and control layout rules are specified; the authors note cross-experiment normalization and single-cell statistical analysis protocols remained open problems at publication.
primary_claim: A complete Nature Protocols workflow for the Cell Painting assay covering design, perturbation, six-dye five-channel staining, high-throughput imaging, illumination correction, QC and about-1,500-feature morphological profiling, validated at two independent sites.

workflow_title: Preparation and deposition of biological imaging data to a public archive with REMBI-standard metadata
occupation_scope: Image data steward; imaging scientist; laboratory bioinformatician preparing publication or project imaging datasets
workflow_summary: Prepare an imaging study for FAIR public release by selecting the right public archive (BioImage Archive for general microscopy data, EMPIAR for electron-microscopy raw images, curated resources like Cell-IDR where applicable), assembling community-recommended REMBI metadata describing the study, samples, instrument and analysis, validating against the archive's submission schema, uploading, and obtaining a citable accession linked from the publication.
source_reference: Primary: Sarkans U et al., 'REMBI: Recommended Metadata for Biological Images - enabling reuse of microscopy data in biology', Nat Methods 18(12):1418-1422 (2021), DOI 10.1038/s41592-021-01166-8, PMID 34021280, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8606015/ (fetched HTTP 200, full text read through the archive-history section): draft metadata guidelines from EMBL-EBI and community representatives (Hinxton workshop, October 2019) for light and electron microscopy, stating that systematic archiving of data plus metadata in public databases is the prerequisite for reuse, that metadata must describe the experiment, samples and instrument, and detailing the archive landscape (BioImage Archive established July 2019 at EMBL-EBI, EMPIAR since 2013, Cell-IDR/Tissue-IDR, SSBD, Cell Image Library, Brain Image Library). Supporting: BioImage Archive https://www.ebi.ac.uk/bioimage-archive (cited directly by the primary as the EMBL-EBI deposition archive for microscopy images associated with peer-reviewed publications); EMPIAR metadata schema http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/emtest/empiar/schema (cited directly by the primary as the de facto standard for that community).
expert_raw_materials: Raw and derived image datasets of potentially multi-terabyte size, acquisition and sample-preparation records, analysis results and code, archive submission templates, ORCID and grant identifiers, any consent or data-access records tied to the samples.
usage_permissions: Deposition requires that the submitter holds the rights to release the data and, for human-derived material, that consent and ethics terms permit public sharing; published datasets are released under the archive's terms (BioImage Archive and EMPIAR are EMBL-EBI public resources); specialized resources have their own access policies.
task_input: An imaging study near publication or project closure: raw and derived image files, laboratory metadata records, and associated analysis outputs.
professional_operations: Select the target archive (BioImage Archive for general light-microscopy data, EMPIAR for electron-microscopy and cryo raw images, curated resources such as Cell-IDR for reference atlases); assemble REMBI metadata across experiment, sample, instrument and analysis categories; validate against the archive-specific submission schema; upload files through the submission system; complete curatorial review with archive staff; obtain an accession and DOI; reference the accession from the publication; keep access terms and embargos consistent with consent and funder mandates.
expected_deliverable: A publicly citable archived imaging dataset with accession and DOI, complete REMBI-based metadata, discoverable through the archive's search interface or API.
success_criteria: The dataset is findable and accessible via the archive API; metadata is complete enough that a third party can interpret the experiment and reuse the images; the publication links to the accession; curators accept the submission.
verification_approach: Archive curation review (the BioImage Archive performs submission curation per the primary's workshop history); download a test file back and verify integrity; confirm metadata renders in the archive interface and API; independent re-analysis of a sample dataset.
platform_dependencies: The EMBL-EBI submission systems and file-transfer channels (the EMPIAR schema endpoint is served over FTP per the primary); high-volume storage and internet bandwidth; web submission interfaces; institutional data-management plans.
blocking_risks: Multi-terabyte transfer and storage costs; the metadata assembly burden grows with each required element (flagged by the authors); human-derived data may require regulated-access handling or embargos; community-specific schemas are still evolving (the primary reports the EMPIAR model was still being expanded); REMBI was published as a draft to be implemented, so what is enforced differs by archive.
expert_capability: A data steward who understands imaging metadata semantics, archive schemas, and the legal/consent boundary of what may be made public.
cross_domain_overlap: Cryo-EM raw-image deposition in EMPIAR also serves the biomolecular EMDB deposition workflow (life_biomol_wf02), but that row covers structure validation and map deposition while this row covers general biological-image archiving and metadata curation; QUAREP WG7 (life_cellimg_wf02) supplies the QC metadata consumed here; genomics has parallel deposit workflows (life_genom_wf01 data sharing) with different archives and schemas.
granularity_check: Proper granularity: a bounded per-study deposition task recurring across publications, not a career (being an archive curator) and not a micro-action (uploading one file).
pending_confirmation: REMBI is presented by its authors as a draft proposal to be implemented and discussed (abstract). Confirm with EMBL-EBI BioImage Archive curator staff which REMBI elements are now enforced in submissions and whether EMPIAR tiering changed; E3 because the standard's operative status is transitional and the workflow chain was assembled from the paper plus archive documentation cited by it.
data_usage_authorization: E3 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8606015/): deposition is premised on the submitter holding release rights and, for human-derived data, on consent and ethics terms permitting public sharing; BioImage Archive and EMPIAR releases are governed by EMBL-EBI public-resource terms; the archive URLs were cited directly by the primary.
privacy_considerations: E1 (https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/): human-derived images, especially with donor or clinical metadata, are personal (health) data under GDPR Art 4(1)/4(15) in the EU and governed by HIPAA where US clinical; de-identification or regulated access is required before public release; pure cell-line image data without donor linkage is not personal data.
research_ethics: E1 (https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/): studies producing human-tissue images require research-ethics-committee approval (2024 Helsinki para 23) and consent covering data storage and secondary use (para 32); animal-derived imaging follows institutional animal-welfare approvals (para 21); deposition must not exceed the consented scope.
reproducibility_assessment: E3 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8606015/): the workflow exists to make imaging data FAIR and reusable; REMBI standardizes metadata across archives, and stable accessions/DOIs support citation-driven reuse; what remains less standardized are modality-specific community schemas still under development.
primary_claim: Draft consensus metadata guidelines (REMBI) produced by EMBL-EBI with light- and electron-microscopy community representatives specifying that experiment, sample, instrument and analysis information must accompany biological image data in public archives (BioImage Archive, EMPIAR) to make it FAIR and reusable.
